fields.mechanism: Non-linear dynamic coupling between cam rotation, flat-faced follower, and guide clearances produces friction- and impact-driven follower motion that deviates from the ideal kinematic profile.
fields.intervention: Fit the 16 mm flat-faced cam followers with precisely toleranced guide bushings that minimize radial clearance while preserving the certified cam profile and follower diameter class, and use the Solidworks-based non-linear clearance simulation from the paper to size the bushing clearance and friction so the follower’s actual trajectory matches the ideal profile at 420 cpm.
fields.expected_effect: Reduced impact loading and frictional contact-stress excursions at the flat face lower Hertzian stress cycling, extending spalling life from 6–9 weeks past the one-week maintenance interval and reducing metal-debris generation on the food-contact side.
fields.falsification_test: Run the folding station at 420 cpm, 20 h/day with the reworked bushings, and monitor weekly for 12 weeks using surface profilometry and lubricant-particle counting; if any follower shows a fatigue spall or a statistically significant rise in metallic debris before week 12, the mechanism is falsified.

fields.mechanism: Dynamic impact and friction between cam, flat-faced follower, and guides during uniform-velocity rotation, with clearance-driven non-linear follower motion that governs contact-stress accumulation on the follower face.
fields.intervention: Use the paper's non-linear dynamic framework to characterize the actual follower displacement (including guide-clearance effects) at the certified 420 cpm cam speed, and add small compliant pre-load elements (wave washers or micro-shim stacks) on the fixed studs to take up the guide clearance and reduce the impact/friction loading on the 16 mm flat follower face — keeping cam profile and follower diameter class unchanged.
fields.expected_effect: Reduced impact loading and friction at the cam-follower contact lowers the Hertzian contact-stress cycling that drives surface fatigue spalling, extending spall life well beyond 6–9 weeks and suppressing metal-debris generation so weekly maintenance becomes feasible.
fields.falsification_test: Run two identical folding stations on the packaging line for 8 weeks at 420 cpm, 20 h/day; the station with the pre-loaded (clearance-compensated) followers must show no spalls > 1 mm² on the follower faces and a measurable reduction in lubricant iron content (e.g., >50% drop in ppm Fe vs. the unmodified station), and spectrogram/Lyapunov-exponent analysis of the follower motion must show reduced non-linear vibration amplitude relative to the baseline station.

fields.mechanism: Clearance-induced impact and friction between the cam, the flat-faced follower, and the guide surfaces drives non-linear follower motion that intensifies surface contact loading on the follower face.
fields.intervention: Measure and minimize the clearance between each 16 mm flat-faced follower and its guide on the folding station's fixed stud, and add a thin compliant/damping shim (e.g., elastomer-backed wear plate) at the follower-to-guide interface so that follower-face contact loading during the 420 cycles/min rotation reflects the low-clearance, friction- and impact-attenuated regime analyzed in the paper.
fields.expected_effect: Reduced impact forces and contact-stress concentrations at the flat follower face lower the Hertzian contact fatigue driving force, extending spall initiation past the required ≥1 week maintenance interval while preserving the certified cam profile and 16 mm follower class.
fields.falsification_test: Run the folding station at 420 cycles/min for 20 h/day with the modified followers and inspect follower faces weekly; if spalls reappear within 6–9 weeks (or contact-load/strain measurements on the follower face remain at pre-modification levels), the clearance/friction attenuation mechanism is falsified for this duty cycle.

fields.mechanism: Non-linear dynamic interaction between a rotating cam and a flat-faced follower, governed by clearances between the follower and its guides, which causes impact, friction, and chaotic (largest Lyapunov exponent) follower motion that drives surface fatigue on the follower face.
fields.intervention: Retain the certified cam profile, 16 mm flat-faced follower diameter, and 420 cycles per minute, but deliberately set the flat-faced follower-to-guide clearance at the value the paper identifies as smoothing impact (rather than minimizing clearance), and add a micro-damping/guide-liner material tuned to the Lyapunov-regime follower oscillation frequencies the paper's non-linear analysis predicts; verify the cam-follower y-direction motion with the paper's high-resolution optical-marker follower-stem measurement method to confirm reduced impact-driven follower excursions before re-installing in the folding station.
fields.expected_effect: Reduced per-cycle impact velocity and chaotic lateral excursion of the flat-faced follower against the cam face, lowering the Hertzian contact-stress cycling that initiates subsurface fatigue crack nucleation and spalling, extending follower life well beyond the 6–9 week interval and keeping metal-debris contamination of the food-contact zone below weekly-maintenance detection limits.
fields.falsification_test: Instrument one folding-station stud with the paper's high-resolution optical marker on the follower stem, measure the y-direction follower motion and compute the largest Lyapunov exponent under the production 420 cpm, 20 h/day cycle; the intervention passes only if the measured Lyapunov exponent and peak impact velocity are both statistically lower (paired runs, n ≥ 10 production days) than the pre-intervention baseline, and only if no follower spalling is observed at the next two scheduled weekly inspections.
fields.mechanism_source_span: A mechanism with a cam and a flat-faced follower is considered for distinct angular velocities. The dynamic analysis presents follower linkage displacement driven by a cam rotating at a uniform angular velocity. The system has clearances between the flat-faced follower and the guides and the effect of clearance is analyzed.

fields.mechanism: Non-linear dynamic coupling of clearance, impact, and friction between the cam and the flat-faced follower governs the follower's actual motion and contact loading.
fields.intervention: Measure or simulate the existing folding station's cam-flat-faced-follower linkage for the non-linear effects reported in the paper — specifically the clearance between follower and guides, the impact at cam-follower engagement, and the friction at the cam-follower and follower-guide contacts — and then reduce those dynamic contact loads by adjusting follower/guide clearance and guide surface finish within the existing 16 mm flat-faced follower class, while keeping the certified cam profile.
fields.expected_effect: Lowered cyclic impact and friction loading on the 16 mm flat-faced follower face extends the spalling life beyond the required once-per-week maintenance interval at 420 cycles per minute, reducing metallic debris reaching the food-contact zone.
fields.falsification_test: Run the cam-follower linkage at the certified 420 cpm with the adjusted clearance/guide finish on a qualification rig and compare measured follower face impact and friction loading against the baseline non-linear dynamic analysis; if follower face fatigue spalling still recurs within 6-9 weeks under equivalent loading, the mechanism is falsified.
